summary: Intermittent 429s observed after migrating high-volume webhook fleet to new burst-pool policy
description:
Issue summary:
Streamline Analytics reported intermittent 429 responses from the Redwood API beginning immediately after a scheduled migration that moved their high-throughput webhook fleet onto a new 'compressed-burst' burst-pool policy. The behavior started at the end of a rolling route-weight change and appears correlated with signed URL fanout and connection reuse at edge proxies.

Impact:
Approximately 6–12% of webhook deliveries returned 429s during the migration window, impacting downstream processing pipelines and causing retries and duplicate records. Customer is on a Dedicated plan and reports business impact to ETL reliability and SLA flashes.

Observed behavior:
- 429s returned with X-RateLimit-Reason: burst_pool_overdraft or X-RateLimit-Reason: soft_window_exhaust
- Throttles appear to affect only webhook endpoints that use short-lived signed URLs and multiplexed keepalive connections to the edge (HTTP/2).
- Errors spike during the migration flip of route weights and then partially subside but recur for specific API keys.

Expected behavior:
- Migration to burst-pool policy should not cause opaque 429 spikes; bulk warmups should be accounted against migration ramp and not double-count per-connection preflight checks.

Customer visible evidence supplied:
- Request IDs + timestamps: list provided in support attachment (S3 link)
- Raw headers showing X-RateLimit-* headers and signed-url signature fields
- Short curl reproducer provided showing intermittent 429 for same API key when reusing an http2 connection
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Obtain a short-lived signed URL for webhook call using customer's API key and signature scheme
2) Open an HTTP/2 persistent connection (keepalive) to the edge and send a sequence of parallel POSTs using the same signed URL with very short TTLs
3) Observe repeated 429 responses during a background change of route weight (simulated by toggling a test route via the console),
4) Repeat with fresh non-signed API key and note reduced throttle incidence (illustrates signed-url accounting surface area)

comments: 2026-02-28 - Eliana Park (Support): Customer opened with detailed curl reproducer and sample headers. Noted immediate correlation with migration period and signed-url use.
2026-02-28 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Acknowledged and started triage. Requested packet captures and list of affected request_ids. Added rate-limiter and ingress teams to the ticket.

2026-02-28 - SRE (investigation): Early hypothesis: double-accounting of signed-url preflight across edge and origin when connection reuse occurs. Edge records preflight and origin also counts a refill for the same logical request during route handoff. Linking troubleshooting playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/rate-limiter-dedupe
2026-03-01 - Customer (Streamline Analytics): Provided additional request_ids and noted that increasing signed-url TTL from 10s to 60s temporarily reduced 429s but did not eliminate them.

2026-03-01 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Observed a surge pattern when route-weight changes cause a fraction of requests to be re-routed mid-connection. Filed a quick mitigation (rollback of compressed-burst policy for the customer's tenant at 2026-03-01T02:15Z).
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: 429 spike aligns with compressed-burst pool allocation events and route-weight flip timestamps (console audit logs)
Reproducer: Local reproducer using http2 keepalive + signed-url rapidly toggling route weight produced 40% 429s in 5 minutes (highly deterministic)

Hypothesis A: Signed-url preflight is being counted twice when an edge proxy forwards a preflight probe and the origin also treats it as a new token consumption because the route mapping changed mid-TTL

Hypothesis B: Edge connection reuse causes per-connection token-window invariants to leak between routes; refill calculation uses per-connection counter plus per-key bucket leading to faster depletion
Related artifacts: linked_prs and postmortem references attached below
workaround: Rolled back compressed-burst policy on the customer's dedicated pool and advised the customer to stagger webhook fleet migrations and increase signed-url TTL to 60s as a temporary mitigation.
resolution: In progress - temporary rollback completed (2026-03-01). Long-term fix drafted: de-dupe preflight accounting in the ingress proxy (only count signed-url consumption once per logical request id) and add a short grace window during route-weight handoffs. Patch PR opened and under review.
